feedback: This is written before the candidate has raced. Iteration 0 is the only evidence. All 60 trials ended off-track with max_error of 0.062 to 0.069 and line_loss_events of 1 to 2, while steering oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.15). So the problem is coverage, not jitter, which supports widening the array as you proposed. I have built the controller for your widened array with kp 3.0 and kd 0.1, a modest increase to correct drift harder. The next race will decide the next change. If line_loss_events is still above 0 on the slalom or s-bend while max_error is at or above 0.06, the array is still too narrow for the sharpest bends. Next, move the sensors forward to y = 0.04 m to shorten the lead. If the robot holds the line (max_error below 0.06, line_loss_events at 0) but completion_time is above 3.0 s, the limit is speed, so reduce mass or raise wheel_radius. If steering_oscillation rises sharply, the higher kp is too aggressive, so return to kp 2.5 before changing geometry.
requested_changes: If the next race still shows line_loss_events > 0 or max_error >= 0.06 on the slalom or s-bend, move all sensors to y = 0.04 m (keep x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 and sensor_size 0.016). Iteration 0 showed the off-track limit is reached at the 50 mm lead, so a shorter lead lets the controller react sooner.

If the next race keeps the line (max_error < 0.06, line_loss_events 0) but completion_time stays above 3.0 s, reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg or raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m. Iteration 0 shows speed-limited progress at 0.10 to 0.15 with no completions, so the bottleneck is also likely speed.

If the next race shows steering_oscillation rising well above the iteration 0 range (0.07 to 0.15), keep the same geometry and reduce kp to 2.5 with kd at 0.1. Iteration 0 oscillation was low, so the higher gain is only useful if the array keeps the tape in view.
